test_title: PYST 23 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 20 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Identify the voice (active or passive) and tense of the verb phrase "are intended" in the sentence:

"These examinations, which demand years of rigorous preparation, are intended to select only the most capable candidates."
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3** i.e '**Passive voice, simple present**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb phrase **"are intended"** is in the passive voice, which means the subject is receiving the action of the verb.
 
• **In the simple present tense,** the passive voice is formed by using the present tense of the verb "to be" (am, is, are) followed by the past participle of the main verb.
 
• In this case, "are" is the present tense of the verb "to be", and "intended" is the past participle of the main verb "intend".

Therefore, the **correct answer** is- **Option 3.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active voice:** In an active voice sentence, the subject performs the action expressed by the verb. "These examinations select..." is an example of the active voice. 
 
• **Present perfect:** The present perfect tense is formed with "have/has" + the past participle of the verb. For example, "have intended" or "has intended".
 
• **Past perfect:** The past perfect tense is formed with "had" + the past participle of the verb. For example, "had intended".
